name: Vyazma
summary: Davout's I Corps, the rearguard of the retreating army, had fallen far behind when Miloradovich's advance guard struck the road between it and Eugène's and Ney's corps before Vyazma. Eugène and Poniatowski turned back to open the way, and the French fought their way through to the town; Paskevich's and Choglokov's men stormed into Vyazma behind them as it burned, and the French lost some 6,000 men, and their order.

forces.name: Compans's Division
forces.summary: Davout's rearguard division, cut off from the rest of the army when Miloradovich's cavalry came down on the road; it fought its way forward to Vyazma as the Russians pressed on all sides.
notes: By now the French divisions were a fraction of their strength, a few hundred to a few thousand men; the formation is as Nafziger gives it earlier in the campaign, so mark battalions Small or leave some out to suit.
Compans is the book's named commander.
Only the 61st is recorded in the fighting; the rest of the division stood in reserve.
The horse battery, without three cavalry regiments in the force, shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named General de Division Compans, with his own rating.
